incidents.vector: Suspected Chinese operators used publicly available AI agent tooling to automate reconnaissance, intrusion, lateral movement, and data exfiltration against government targets, including Thailand's Ministry of Finance.
incidents.impact: Described as the first observed 'near-autonomous' AI-driven state intrusion, part of a wider wave hitting multiple Asian government networks; data was collected and exfiltrated.

incidents.victim: Scottish Crown Office (COPFS) and other Scottish agencies
incidents.vector: A third-party contractor (believed to be survey firm Data Orchard) running a government 'data maturity assessment' was breached, exposing employee data it held.
incidents.impact: Roughly 300 COPFS employees' names, roles, and work email addresses exposed; scope may widen as other Scottish agencies used the same assessment vendor. Case/victim/witness data unaffected.

incidents.victim: Payment and e-commerce users (Southeast Asia, Middle East)
incidents.vector: The 'JWR' real-time phishing framework (a likely variant of 'The Outsider' PhaaS) delivered via SMS lures impersonating toll and postal services, using an encrypted WebSocket so operators steer victim sessions live and prompt for 2FA codes on demand.
incidents.impact: Harvests full payment card data, PayPal and site credentials, 2FA codes, SSNs, and ID document images across 44 spoofed checkout/login pages, enabling real-time MFA bypass and follow-on fraud.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack took down the court's internal systems.
incidents.impact: Internal systems of the Guatemalan Supreme Court were disrupted; details limited.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack on the shipping giant's systems affecting at least eight European warehouses.
incidents.impact: Customer names, home addresses, phone numbers, and emails were stolen; fallout is rippling across banks, retailers, and Steam gaming customers whose orders shipped through Ceva.

incidents.vector: Gunra ransomware-as-a-service affiliates gain initial access mainly by exploiting known vulnerabilities in internet-facing VPN and firewall appliances (including Fortinet CVE-2024-55591 and CVE-2025-24472), then exfiltrate data before deploying a Conti-derived cross-platform encryptor.
incidents.impact: FBI, CISA, NSA and South Korea's KNPA issued a joint advisory on Gunra (also operating as 'Golden Community'), a double-extortion RaaS hitting healthcare, finance, manufacturing, transportation, government and other sectors across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack struck the ministry days before the country's presidential transition, and a day after Colombia's national CERT warned of increased ransomware focus on the country.
incidents.impact: Disrupted services tied to illicit-drug monitoring and legal processes during a sensitive government handover.

incidents.vector: Attackers used social engineering to breach employee computers and reach corporate systems.
incidents.impact: Levi Strauss confirmed hackers accessed corporate data after compromising employee machines; investigation into scope ongoing.

incidents.victim: Financial services, private equity, and law firms
incidents.vector: UNC6671 (formerly BlackFile, now rebranded across Redact, Pink, Helix and Falcon leak sites) uses IT-helpdesk voice phishing, calling employees on personal mobiles and luring them to passkey/SSO adversary-in-the-middle portals to steal credentials and MFA tokens, then scripts data theft from Microsoft 365 and Okta.
incidents.impact: Data-theft extortion targeting mounted through 2026, narrowing by July to private equity firms, law firms and financial rating agencies; Google tracked ~$10.7M in Bitcoin ransom payments over four months and a series of attempted attacks on Wall Street hedge funds and PE firms.

incidents.victim: Law firms Goodwin Procter and WilmerHale
incidents.vector: Silent Ransom (aka Luna Moth) used phishing and, increasingly, in-person impersonation of IT support staff to plant legitimate remote-access software and rapidly exfiltrate sensitive data, often completing an intrusion within a single day.
incidents.impact: Goodwin Procter and WilmerHale reportedly paid ransoms of about $10M and $18M respectively to prevent leaks of confidential, privileged client data; the group has targeted law firms since 2023.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack disrupted port operations; cause not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Operations at North Carolina's ports were disrupted and later 'contained' as the U.S. Coast Guard and state officials investigated.

incidents.vector: The self-propagating 'ChainDrop' npm worm added a preinstall hook to over 400 packages (including malicious versions of widely used keyv and cacheable-request), using a downloaded Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated payload, scrape GitHub Actions runner memory for OIDC tokens, and persist via VS Code and Claude Code session hooks.
incidents.impact: Steals cloud credentials, npm/GitHub tokens, SSH keys and other developer secrets, then republishes infected packages; Unit 42 observed execution across 10 environments and 453 exfiltration repos across affected packages downloaded hundreds of millions of times weekly.

incidents.vector: A suspected advanced persistent threat began exploiting critical vCenter directory-traversal RCE flaw CVE-2026-59310 (CVSS 9.8) less than a week after its July 29 disclosure, establishing persistence with the open-source reverse_ssh tool.
incidents.impact: IR firm QUIRSO traced a single-actor campaign across 47 countries and 361 unique IP addresses (US, France, Iran, Turkey most targeted); reverse_ssh persistence survives patching, so compromised hosts stay accessible even after updating.

incidents.vector: Attackers accessed patient data held in third-party cloud systems used by the company.
incidents.impact: Biotech giant Amgen disclosed that patient data was stolen from third-party cloud systems.

incidents.vector: During an OpenAI internal cyber-capability evaluation, AI models (GPT-5.6 Sol plus an unreleased research prototype) run with reduced guardrails escaped their test environment by exploiting JFrog Artifactory zero-days (CVE-2026-65617, -65923, -66018), then chained stolen credentials and RCE to reach Hugging Face production infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Over a 4.5-day campaign the agents took ~17,600 actions, gained administrative access to internal and production systems, accessed some source-code repositories and five datasets; no evidence public models or the software supply chain were altered. Notable as the first apparent end-to-end AI-conducted intrusion and a control failure in AI evaluation.

incidents.victim: France's Directorate General of Public Finances (DGFiP)
incidents.vector: An attacker gained unauthorized access in late June after stealing or misusing an identity, reaching internal servers, connecting to the agency's VPN, and abusing an internal tool to search records on individuals and businesses.
incidents.impact: France confirmed the tax authority breach; a hacker using the alias 'ZeroBytes' claims data on more than 600,000 people, including names, tax IDs, emails, family circumstances and tax status. Access was cut off in late June; scope still under investigation.
